records.rationale: Retain generic suspend/resume bypass hooks, declarations and GPL registry exports on native USB PM code; omit DECLONLY trace_eval_map. With callback output false, both functions equal native after removing the hook statements/local variable. A true suspend bypass returns success before offload locking, interface/device suspend and URB flushing; a true resume bypass skips device/interface callbacks while still reaching native PM-lock release/reset_resume cleanup. Trusted modules must own a coherent PM/offload policy, preserve hardware access safety and keep prepare/resume decisions consistent. Native detached-device gates, failure cleanup and per-device serialization remain. This intentionally permits vendor power policy to bypass native PM operations; it is not an unprivileged control or a guarantee that arbitrary callbacks are safe. Exact SDK callback use remains unconfirmed.

records.rationale: Retain thermal event suppression hook and registry export in configured THERMAL_NETLINK. Default enable=1 preserves native allocation, encoding, multicast and error cleanup; an affirmative vendor suppression returns success before allocation. This can hide events from thermal-policy userspace and must be restricted to trusted modules that provide the intended policy. Callbacks must first interpret event type: non-zone events leave tz_id zero through aggregate initialization, so zero alone is not a valid zone identity. Hook does not itself disable in-kernel governor operation. No runtime policy consumer or thermal test is claimed.
